name: ADHD
summary: Neurodevelopmental condition involving developmentally inappropriate, impairing inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity across settings.
assessment: Assess childhood onset, functional impairment, history across settings, sleep, mood, learning and substance factors.
caution: Symptoms alone are insufficient; DSM-5-TR requires multiple criteria and onset of several symptoms before age 12.

name: Adjustment disorder
summary: Emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable stressor, with distress or impairment disproportionate to context.
assessment: Establish timing relative to the stressor, functioning, cultural context and alternative disorders.
caution: Symptoms typically begin within three months of the stressor; consider whether another disorder better explains the presentation.

name: Alcohol withdrawal
summary: Autonomic and neuropsychiatric syndrome after reduction or cessation of sustained heavy alcohol use.
assessment: Ask about drinking history, timing, tremor, sweating, agitation, seizures, hallucinations and vital signs.
caution: Seizures and delirium tremens can be life-threatening and require urgent medical care.

name: ALS
summary: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a progressive motor neuron disease affecting upper and lower motor neuron pathways.
assessment: Assess progressive weakness, atrophy, fasciculations, spasticity, bulbar and respiratory function; exclude mimics.
caution: Sensory loss is not usually a dominant feature; diagnosis requires specialist clinical assessment and often EMG.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Alzheimer-related logopenic PPA
summary: Language-led neurodegenerative syndrome with word-finding pauses and impaired sentence repetition; Alzheimer pathology is a common cause.
assessment: Evaluate naming, repetition, phonological working memory, neuropsychology, MRI and, when appropriate, biomarkers.
caution: Logopenic primary progressive aphasia is a syndrome; Alzheimer pathology should not be assumed without supportive evidence.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Anxiety
summary: A normal emotional state of apprehension or threat anticipation that can also occur in medical and psychiatric disorders.
assessment: Explore triggers, duration, avoidance, physical symptoms, impairment and medical or substance causes.
caution: Anxiety itself is a symptom, not a specific anxiety disorder.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: anxiety disorder
summary: Umbrella term for disorders involving excessive fear or anxiety and associated avoidance or impairment.
assessment: Characterize the feared situations, time course, functional impact and alternative medical causes.
caution: Panic disorder, phobias, generalized anxiety disorder and other anxiety disorders have different criteria.

name: aphasic stroke
summary: Stroke affecting language networks, often in the dominant cerebral hemisphere, causing sudden language impairment.
assessment: Urgently assess onset time, language, other deficits and brain/vascular imaging.
caution: Sudden aphasia is a stroke emergency until proven otherwise; seizures and migraine can mimic it.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: ARFID
summary: Avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder: insufficient intake due to sensory aversion, low interest or fear of consequences, without weight/shape disturbance driving restriction.
assessment: Assess growth, nutrition, deficiencies, psychosocial impact and exclusion of medical or cultural explanations.
caution: Unlike anorexia nervosa, restriction is not primarily motivated by fear of weight gain.

name: arrhythmia
summary: Abnormal cardiac rhythm that may cause palpitations, dizziness, fainting or instability.
assessment: Assess pulse, ECG, symptom rhythm correlation, medications, electrolytes and cardiac risk.
caution: Syncope with chest pain, exertion or family history of sudden death warrants urgent assessment.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: arterial stroke
summary: Acute ischemic brain injury caused by interruption of arterial blood flow.
assessment: Record last-known-well time; urgent stroke evaluation with brain and vascular imaging.
caution: Sudden focal deficit requires emergency care; reperfusion eligibility is time-dependent.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: autoimmune encephalitis
summary: Inflammatory brain syndrome mediated by immune mechanisms, potentially causing subacute memory, behavioral, seizure or movement symptoms.
assessment: Assess subacute evolution, MRI, EEG, CSF, antibody testing and infectious mimics in specialist care.
caution: Normal early MRI or negative antibody tests do not necessarily exclude the diagnosis; infection must be evaluated.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: avoidant personality traits
summary: Persistent tendencies toward social inhibition and fear of criticism that may be subclinical.
assessment: Explore duration, context, distress, interpersonal goals and functional impact.
caution: Traits alone do not establish avoidant personality disorder.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: B12 deficiency
summary: Low vitamin B12 causing hematologic, neurological and cognitive manifestations, sometimes without anemia.
assessment: Check B12 status, blood count and relevant confirmatory tests; evaluate diet, absorption and neurological signs.
caution: Untreated neurological damage may persist; normal blood count does not exclude neurological involvement.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: bipolar depression
summary: Depressive episode occurring in a person with bipolar disorder, often clinically resembling unipolar depression.
assessment: Ask specifically about past mania/hypomania, medications, substances, safety and longitudinal course.
caution: A current depressive episode cannot establish bipolar disorder without relevant mood episode history.

name: bipolar depression with psychotic features
summary: Bipolar depressive episode accompanied by delusions or hallucinations.
assessment: Confirm depressive episode, bipolar history, psychosis timing and urgent safety risks.
caution: Psychosis occurring independently of mood episodes broadens the differential to schizoaffective and primary psychotic disorders.

name: Bipolar disorder
summary: Mood disorder spectrum characterized by episodes of mania and/or hypomania, often with depression.
assessment: Obtain longitudinal mood, energy, sleep, activity, impairment and treatment history.
caution: Bipolar I requires mania; bipolar II involves hypomania and major depression without past mania.

name: Bipolar disorder with psychotic features
summary: Bipolar disorder in which psychotic symptoms occur during mood episodes.
assessment: Establish whether psychosis is confined to mania or depression and assess risk.
caution: Psychosis during an elevated episode makes that episode manic, not hypomanic.

name: bipolar mania
summary: Manic episode with abnormally elevated or irritable mood and increased activity or energy, plus characteristic associated changes.
assessment: Assess duration, sleep need, speech, judgment, risk, impairment and substance or medical causes.
caution: A full manic episode generally lasts at least one week or any duration if hospitalization is necessary.

name: bipolar psychosis
summary: Informal label for psychotic symptoms occurring during a bipolar mood episode.
assessment: Document exact relationship between mood and psychotic symptoms.
caution: Not a separate DSM-5-TR diagnosis; classify the underlying bipolar episode with psychotic features.

name: botulism
summary: Neuroparalytic illness due to botulinum toxin impairing neuromuscular transmission.
assessment: Urgently assess descending weakness, cranial nerves, swallowing, breathing and exposure history.
caution: A medical emergency; pupils and autonomic findings may help distinguish it from myasthenia gravis.

sources.title: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — Health Topics
U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Brain metastasis
summary: Secondary brain tumor resulting from cancer spreading from another organ.
assessment: Assess cancer history, focal signs, seizures and contrast MRI; coordinate oncology workup.
caution: Multiple lesions suggest but do not prove metastases; tissue diagnosis may be necessary.

sources.title: U.S. National Cancer Institute — Adult CNS Tumors
U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Cervical radiculopathy
summary: Irritation or compression of a cervical nerve root causing neck/arm pain and segmental sensory or motor symptoms.
assessment: Examine myotomes, reflexes, dermatomes and red flags; image selectively.
caution: Differentiate from peripheral entrapment and cervical myelopathy.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: chronic pain with adaptive coping
summary: Persistent pain accompanied by effective coping strategies and maintained functioning; this is not a disease diagnosis.
assessment: Assess pain mechanism, interference, mood, sleep and functional goals.
caution: Adaptive coping does not imply pain is unreal or exclude treatable pathology.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: circadian rhythm disorder
summary: Sleep-wake disturbance from mismatch between internal circadian timing and desired schedule.
assessment: Use sleep history, diaries, actigraphy when indicated, and evaluate shift work or light exposure.
caution: Distinguish from insufficient sleep and primary insomnia.

name: Copper deficiency
summary: Nutritional or absorption-related deficiency that can produce anemia, neutropenia and myeloneuropathy.
assessment: Assess serum copper/ceruloplasmin, zinc exposure, gastrointestinal history and spinal cord findings.
caution: Can resemble B12-related myelopathy; excess zinc is a potential cause.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: cranial neuropathy
summary: Dysfunction of one or more cranial nerves affecting eye movements, facial function, sensation, hearing or swallowing.
assessment: Localize affected nerve(s), onset, associated deficits and consider imaging/infectious workup.
caution: This is a localization category, not one disease; multiple nerves may suggest a skull-base or meningeal process.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Dementia
summary: Acquired cognitive decline severe enough to interfere with independent daily function, due to various causes.
assessment: Assess cognition, function, onset, delirium, depression, medication effects and reversible contributors.
caution: Dementia is a clinical syndrome, not synonymous with Alzheimer disease.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Depression
summary: Low mood or diminished interest that may be a symptom, episode or component of multiple conditions.
assessment: Assess duration, anhedonia, neurovegetative changes, function, bipolar history and suicide risk.
caution: A depressive symptom is not necessarily major depressive disorder.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Depressive disorder
summary: Umbrella category encompassing disorders with clinically significant depressive symptoms and impairment.
assessment: Determine episode duration, severity, recurrence, developmental context and medical causes.
caution: Specific diagnoses such as major depressive disorder and persistent depressive disorder have distinct requirements.

name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
summary: Acute metabolic emergency with ketonemia and acidosis caused by relative or absolute insulin deficiency.
assessment: Urgent glucose, blood ketones, blood gas, electrolytes and precipitant evaluation.
caution: DKA can occur with only modest glucose elevation, including with SGLT2 inhibitor use.

sources.title: American Diabetes Association — Standards of Care
U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: dissociation
summary: Disruption of normal integration of memory, identity, perception, consciousness or experience.
assessment: Clarify depersonalization, derealization, amnesia, trauma, seizures and substances.
caution: Dissociation is a phenomenon, not automatically dissociative identity disorder.

name: DLB
summary: Dementia with Lewy bodies: progressive cognitive syndrome often with fluctuations, visual hallucinations, REM sleep behavior disorder and parkinsonism.
assessment: Assess cognition, sleep, motor findings, medications and supportive biomarkers where appropriate.
caution: Marked antipsychotic sensitivity can occur; distinguish from Parkinson disease dementia using clinical timing.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Drug-induced chorea
summary: Involuntary irregular flowing movements associated with medication or substance exposure.
assessment: Review dopamine-modulating drugs, stimulants, metabolic factors and onset after exposure.
caution: Consider Huntington disease, metabolic disorders and other causes before attributing movements to a drug.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: drug-induced dystonia
summary: Sustained or intermittent muscle contractions producing abnormal postures or twisting, triggered by medication.
assessment: Review recent dopamine-blocking agents and onset; assess airway if neck or throat affected.
caution: Acute laryngeal dystonia can threaten breathing and requires emergency care.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: drug-induced parkinsonism
summary: Bradykinesia with rigidity or tremor associated with dopamine-blocking or dopamine-depleting medication.
assessment: Review exposure and timing, examination and alternative degenerative causes.
caution: Often more symmetric than idiopathic Parkinson disease, but clinical patterns overlap.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: eating disorder
summary: Broad category of persistent eating or feeding disturbances impairing health or psychosocial function.
assessment: Assess intake, weight trajectory, compensatory behavior, medical stability and psychological drivers.
caution: A broad category, not a single diagnosis; ARFID, anorexia, bulimia and binge-eating disorder differ.

name: focal seizure
summary: Seizure beginning in a network limited to one cerebral hemisphere, with variable awareness and motor/sensory manifestations.
assessment: Characterize stereotyped episodes, witness history, EEG and MRI as appropriate.
caution: A single seizure does not automatically establish epilepsy.

sources.title: International League Against Epilepsy — Definition and classification

name: focal seizures
summary: Plural of focal seizure: recurrent or multiple seizures arising in a localized brain network.
assessment: Assess event semiology, frequency, provoking factors, EEG and structural causes.
caution: Focal seizures can spread bilaterally; consider seizure mimics such as syncope.

sources.title: International League Against Epilepsy — Definition and classification

name: functional tic-like behaviors
summary: Tic-like movements or sounds associated with functional neurological symptom mechanisms, often with atypical rapid onset.
assessment: Assess phenomenology, time course, functional impact and coexistence with Tourette syndrome.
caution: Not deliberate or fabricated; diagnosis relies on positive clinical features, not merely normal tests.

name: GAD
summary: Generalized anxiety disorder: excessive difficult-to-control worry across domains with associated symptoms and impairment.
assessment: Assess at least six months of worry in adults, sleep, tension, restlessness, concentration and mimics.
caution: Generalized worry differs from fear restricted to one object or situation.

name: gastrointestinal disorder
summary: Broad term for disease affecting the digestive tract or associated organs.
assessment: Localize symptoms and assess alarm features, nutrition, stool patterns and relevant testing.
caution: Not a single diagnosis; avoid attributing symptoms to anxiety without medical assessment.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: gastrointestinal illness
summary: Nonspecific digestive illness, acute or chronic, infectious or noninfectious.
assessment: Assess hydration, duration, pain, bleeding, fever, medications and exposure history.
caution: Severe abdominal pain, blood loss or dehydration may require urgent care.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Glioma
summary: Diverse primary CNS tumors with glial differentiation and molecularly defined subtypes.
assessment: Assess neurologic symptoms, MRI and neuro-oncology review; tissue and molecular testing may be required.
caution: Imaging appearance alone does not establish tumor grade or molecular subtype.

sources.title: U.S. National Cancer Institute — Adult CNS Tumors
U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: hepatic encephalopathy
summary: Potentially reversible brain dysfunction associated with severe liver disease or portosystemic shunting.
assessment: Assess mental status, precipitating factors, infection, bleeding, constipation and metabolic alternatives.
caution: Ammonia levels alone do not diagnose or grade the syndrome; consider other causes of altered consciousness.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: HSV encephalitis
summary: Herpes simplex virus infection of brain tissue, often affecting temporal lobes and causing fever, seizures and confusion.
assessment: Urgent lumbar puncture with CSF PCR, MRI, EEG and empiric antiviral treatment when suspected.
caution: Potentially fatal without prompt treatment; do not wait for confirmatory PCR to start care when strongly suspected.

sources.title: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — Health Topics
U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Hyperglycemia
summary: Blood glucose above the expected range, due to diabetes, stress physiology, drugs or other causes.
assessment: Confirm glucose, assess symptoms, HbA1c and dehydration or ketosis when indicated.
caution: A laboratory finding rather than a specific disease; severe symptoms can signal DKA or HHS.

sources.title: American Diabetes Association — Standards of Care
U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
summary: Hyperglycemic emergency with marked hyperosmolality and dehydration, usually with minimal significant ketoacidosis.
assessment: Urgent electrolytes, osmolality, glucose, renal function, ketones and mental status.
caution: May overlap with DKA; requires hospital treatment.

sources.title: American Diabetes Association — Standards of Care
U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: hyperthyroidism
summary: Excess thyroid hormone effect causing weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor, palpitations and anxiety-like symptoms.
assessment: Check TSH, free thyroid hormones and cause-specific evaluation.
caution: Thyroid storm is an emergency; do not diagnose an anxiety disorder before considering thyroid disease when indicated.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Hypoglycemia
summary: Abnormally low glucose that may cause sweating, tremor, confusion, seizures or loss of consciousness.
assessment: Check glucose during symptoms and investigate drugs, fasting or systemic causes.
caution: Whipple triad helps confirm clinically important hypoglycemia in people without diabetes; severe episodes require urgent treatment.

sources.title: American Diabetes Association — Standards of Care
U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: hypothyroidism
summary: Insufficient thyroid hormone effect causing fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation, cognitive slowing and other symptoms.
assessment: Measure TSH and free T4; interpret according to pituitary and clinical context.
caution: Symptoms overlap with depression and many non-thyroid conditions.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Intracranial bleed
summary: Bleeding within the skull, including intracerebral, subarachnoid and extra-axial hemorrhage.
assessment: Urgent neurological evaluation and brain imaging, usually noncontrast CT initially.
caution: Thunderclap headache, sudden deficits or altered consciousness require emergency assessment.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: intracranial mass
summary: Space-occupying intracranial lesion, including tumor, abscess, hematoma or other process.
assessment: Evaluate focal deficits, seizures, raised-pressure symptoms and appropriate imaging.
caution: An imaging description, not a specific tumor diagnosis.

sources.title: U.S. National Cancer Institute — Adult CNS Tumors
U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: learning disorder
summary: Persistent difficulty acquiring academic skills despite appropriate instruction, with functional impairment.
assessment: Assess developmental and educational history, standardized academic performance and alternative explanations.
caution: Specific learning disorder is distinct from intellectual disability and insufficient teaching opportunity.

name: Lyme disease
summary: Tick-borne Borrelia infection with variable skin, joint, cardiac and neurological manifestations.
assessment: Use exposure history, examination and stage-appropriate validated serology when indicated.
caution: Testing without compatible clinical context may mislead; facial palsy and meningoradiculitis are possible manifestations.

sources.title: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — Health Topics
U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: medical illness
summary: General label for physical health conditions, not an independent diagnosis.
assessment: Investigate organ-system symptoms and objective abnormalities guided by history and examination.
caution: A placeholder in differential reasoning; replace with a specific diagnosis when supported.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: medical weight loss
summary: Weight reduction attributable to illness, medication or other physiological cause rather than a psychiatric eating disorder.
assessment: Assess trajectory, intake, systemic symptoms, medication and targeted testing.
caution: Unintentional weight loss is a finding; distinguish from intentional dieting or restrictive eating pathology.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: medication-overuse headache
summary: Headache associated with regular overuse of acute headache medication in someone with a pre-existing headache disorder.
assessment: Document headache days, medication days and duration; classify by medication type.
caution: Typically requires headache on at least 15 days/month and overuse for more than three months; thresholds vary by drug class.

name: Meningioma
summary: Usually dural-based neoplasm arising from meningothelial cells; often slow-growing but behavior varies.
assessment: Assess MRI appearance, growth, symptoms and specialist evaluation.
caution: Imaging suggests but cannot always establish histologic grade.

sources.title: U.S. National Cancer Institute — Adult CNS Tumors
U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: meningitis
summary: Inflammation of meninges, often infectious, causing headache, fever, neck stiffness and sometimes altered consciousness.
assessment: Urgent assessment; blood cultures and lumbar puncture when safe, with prompt empiric therapy if bacterial meningitis suspected.
caution: Absence of neck stiffness does not exclude meningitis; bacterial meningitis is an emergency.

sources.title: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — Health Topics
U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: migraine
summary: Primary headache disorder featuring recurrent attacks, often with nausea and light or sound sensitivity.
assessment: Assess stereotyped attacks, frequency, aura and secondary-headache red flags.
caution: Not every headache with nausea is migraine; sudden new thunderclap headache needs urgent evaluation.

name: Migraine aura
summary: Fully reversible focal neurological symptoms, commonly visual, evolving gradually and often preceding migraine headache.
assessment: Clarify gradual spread, sequence, duration and stroke/seizure mimics.
caution: Typical aura commonly lasts 5–60 minutes per individual symptom; sudden negative deficits suggest TIA/stroke.

name: MOGAD
summary: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, inflammatory CNS demyelination causing optic neuritis, myelitis or encephalitis.
assessment: Assess MRI, phenotype, serum MOG-IgG by validated cell-based assay and mimics.
caution: Positive antibodies without compatible syndrome may be misleading; distinct from multiple sclerosis and AQP4-NMOSD.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: mood disorder
summary: Broad clinical category of disorders characterized by pathological changes in mood and associated function.
assessment: Assess depression, mania/hypomania, duration, impairment, substances and medical causes.
caution: Not a specific diagnosis; classify depressive versus bipolar syndromes appropriately.

name: mood disorder with psychotic features
summary: Descriptive term for mood episodes accompanied by delusions or hallucinations.
assessment: Assess episode timing, mood severity and whether psychosis occurs outside mood episodes.
caution: Formal diagnosis requires identifying the underlying mood disorder and episode.

name: MS
summary: Multiple sclerosis: immune-mediated CNS demyelinating disease with lesions disseminated in space and time or equivalent criteria.
assessment: Assess objective neurological attacks, MRI brain/spine, CSF where appropriate and exclusion of mimics.
caution: A nonspecific white-matter MRI finding alone is not MS.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: MSA
summary: Multiple system atrophy, progressive synucleinopathy causing autonomic failure with parkinsonian and/or cerebellar features.
assessment: Assess orthostatic blood pressure, urinary symptoms, gait, motor signs and specialist imaging.
caution: Early prominent autonomic dysfunction and rapid progression can distinguish it from typical Parkinson disease.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Multifocal motor neuropathy
summary: Immune-mediated peripheral motor neuropathy producing asymmetric distal weakness without significant sensory loss.
assessment: Assess distribution, nerve conduction block and other motor neuron disease mimics.
caution: Treatable disorder; distinguish from ALS, which typically has upper motor neuron signs.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: myasthenia
summary: Usually shorthand for myasthenia gravis, autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder causing fatigable weakness.
assessment: Assess fluctuating ocular/bulbar/limb weakness, antibodies and electrophysiology.
caution: Breathing or swallowing weakness may indicate myasthenic crisis and requires emergency care.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: night eating syndrome
summary: Recurrent evening/night food intake with awareness and distress, often associated with sleep and mood difficulties.
assessment: Assess timing, awareness, intake, sleep pattern and other eating disorders.
caution: Diagnostic classification differs across systems; distinguish from sleep-related eating disorder with reduced awareness.

name: NMOSD
summary: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, inflammatory CNS disease often associated with aquaporin-4 antibodies.
assessment: Assess severe optic neuritis, longitudinal myelitis, area postrema symptoms, MRI and serum AQP4-IgG.
caution: Treatment strategies differ from MS; certain MS therapies can worsen NMOSD.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: NPH
summary: Normal pressure hydrocephalus: potentially treatable syndrome of gait disturbance, cognitive impairment and urinary symptoms with ventriculomegaly.
assessment: Assess gait, MRI/CT and specialist CSF drainage testing when appropriate.
caution: Gait impairment often predominates; ventriculomegaly alone does not prove NPH.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Obstructive sleep apnea
summary: Repeated upper-airway collapse during sleep causing disrupted breathing and sleep fragmentation.
assessment: Assess snoring, witnessed apneas, daytime symptoms and objective sleep testing.
caution: Can contribute to fatigue and cognition problems; severity is established by sleep study, not symptoms alone.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: occipital seizure
summary: Focal seizure arising from occipital cortex, often with brief stereotyped visual phenomena.
assessment: Characterize sudden onset, brief duration, EEG and imaging as appropriate.
caution: Visual migraine aura usually develops more gradually and lasts longer.

sources.title: International League Against Epilepsy — Definition and classification

name: OCPD
summary: Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder, enduring rigidity, perfectionism and need for control impairing functioning.
assessment: Assess pervasive pattern from early adulthood, context and impact on relationships/work.
caution: Unlike OCD, OCPD is not defined by intrusive obsessions and compulsions.

name: other substance use disorder
summary: A substance use disorder involving a substance other than the specific one under discussion.
assessment: Identify substance, impaired control, risky use, social impairment and physiological criteria where applicable.
caution: Not all substance exposure or intoxication meets criteria for a substance use disorder.

name: Panic attacks
summary: Abrupt surges of intense fear or discomfort with autonomic and cognitive symptoms.
assessment: Assess onset, peak, recurrence, triggers, cardiac/thyroid causes and substance use.
caution: Panic attacks are a specifier/symptom phenomenon and can occur outside panic disorder.

name: Parkinson disease dementia
summary: Dementia developing in the setting of established Parkinson disease, often with executive, visuospatial and attention deficits.
assessment: Review timeline of parkinsonism and dementia, cognitive function, hallucinations and medications.
caution: Clinical one-year timing convention helps distinguish from dementia with Lewy bodies.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: peripheral neuropathy
summary: Dysfunction of peripheral nerves causing numbness, pain, weakness or autonomic symptoms.
assessment: Assess distribution, reflexes, diabetes, B12, toxins and nerve conduction studies when indicated.
caution: A syndrome with many causes; distinguish polyneuropathy from focal mononeuropathy and radiculopathy.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Pituitary adenoma
summary: Pituitary neuroendocrine tumor, sometimes hormone-secreting or causing visual and endocrine effects.
assessment: Evaluate pituitary hormone axes, visual fields when indicated and pituitary MRI.
caution: Incidental lesions require different assessment from symptomatic hormone excess or compressive tumors.

sources.title: U.S. National Cancer Institute — Adult CNS Tumors
U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Primary CNS lymphoma
summary: Lymphoma primarily arising in brain, spinal cord, eyes or meninges without systemic origin at diagnosis.
assessment: Assess MRI, immune status, ocular involvement and specialist tissue diagnosis.
caution: Corticosteroids before biopsy can obscure diagnosis in some cases; coordinate with specialists.

sources.title: U.S. National Cancer Institute — Adult CNS Tumors
U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Primary psychiatric disorder
summary: Broad description for psychiatric illness not primarily caused by a medical condition or substance.
assessment: Evaluate longitudinal symptoms, medical causes, substance exposure and functional change.
caution: A category, not a definitive diagnosis; avoid assuming symptoms are psychiatric without assessment.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Primary psychosis
summary: Psychotic syndrome not attributable to a substance, medical illness or mood disorder alone.
assessment: Assess delusions, hallucinations, disorganization, duration, functioning and alternatives.
caution: An umbrella term; schizophrenia, delusional disorder and related disorders require separate criteria.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: PSP
summary: Progressive supranuclear palsy, atypical parkinsonian neurodegeneration often involving falls, eye-movement abnormalities and axial rigidity.
assessment: Assess vertical saccades/gaze, postural instability, cognition and specialist imaging.
caution: Early backward falls and vertical gaze dysfunction may distinguish from Parkinson disease.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: psychosis
summary: Syndrome involving impaired reality testing such as delusions or hallucinations.
assessment: Assess safety, onset, mental state, substances, delirium, mood episodes and neurological causes.
caution: A symptom syndrome, not synonymous with schizophrenia.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: psychotic disorder
summary: Diagnostic family involving clinically significant psychotic phenomena.
assessment: Characterize symptom pattern, duration, functioning, mood relationship and etiologies.
caution: Includes primary, substance-induced and medical-condition-related disorders; not one disease.

name: PTSD
summary: Posttraumatic stress disorder after exposure to qualifying trauma with intrusion, avoidance, negative cognition/mood changes and arousal symptoms.
assessment: Assess trauma exposure, symptom clusters, duration, impairment and dissociation.
caution: DSM-5-TR symptoms persist longer than one month; not all post-trauma distress meets PTSD criteria.

name: pure autonomic failure
summary: Neurodegenerative autonomic disorder causing neurogenic orthostatic hypotension without prominent initial motor features.
assessment: Assess standing blood pressure, autonomic testing, medication causes and follow-up for evolving synucleinopathy.
caution: Distinguish from dehydration, drug-related hypotension and multiple system atrophy.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Ramsay Hunt syndrome
summary: Varicella-zoster reactivation involving facial nerve, often causing painful ear vesicles and facial weakness.
assessment: Assess facial nerve, ear/oral lesions, hearing and vestibular symptoms.
caution: Can occur without visible rash; prompt treatment and eye protection are important.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: RCVS
summary: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome, episodic cerebral arterial narrowing often causing recurrent thunderclap headaches.
assessment: Urgent imaging and vascular evaluation; repeat imaging may be needed.
caution: Subarachnoid hemorrhage and other dangerous causes must be excluded first.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: seizure with Todd paresis
summary: Transient focal weakness following an epileptic seizure.
assessment: Assess witnessed seizure, weakness duration, neurological exam, EEG and imaging when indicated.
caution: Postictal weakness can mimic stroke; acute focal weakness still needs emergency stroke evaluation.

sources.title: International League Against Epilepsy — Definition and classification

name: seizures
summary: Transient episodes due to abnormal excessive neuronal activity; manifestations depend on involved networks.
assessment: Assess semiology, provoking factors, witness history, EEG and brain imaging when appropriate.
caution: Seizures can be acute symptomatic; having a seizure is not identical to having epilepsy.

sources.title: International League Against Epilepsy — Definition and classification

name: Separation anxiety disorder
summary: Excessive developmentally inappropriate fear about separation from attachment figures causing impairment.
assessment: Assess duration, developmental stage, school/work avoidance and other anxiety disorders.
caution: DSM-5-TR duration thresholds differ for children and adults.

name: Sleep deprivation
summary: Insufficient sleep duration or quality relative to physiological need.
assessment: Assess sleep opportunity, schedule, medications, mood and sleep disorders.
caution: Not a specific disease; can worsen attention, mood and seizure susceptibility.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: sleep disorder
summary: Broad group of disorders affecting sleep initiation, maintenance, breathing, timing or behavior.
assessment: Characterize symptoms, schedule, daytime impairment and targeted sleep testing.
caution: Insomnia, sleep apnea, parasomnias and circadian disorders require different evaluations.

name: social anxiety
summary: Fear of negative evaluation in social situations, potentially normal or part of social anxiety disorder.
assessment: Assess triggers, avoidance, persistence and impairment.
caution: Social anxiety disorder requires more than occasional shyness or nervousness.

name: specific phobia
summary: Marked, persistent fear of a particular object or situation, causing avoidance or distress out of proportion to actual danger.
assessment: Assess fear trigger, duration, impairment and differential diagnoses.
caution: DSM-5-TR usually requires persistence for at least six months.

name: Spinal cord compression
summary: Pressure on spinal cord producing weakness, sensory changes, gait dysfunction and possible bladder/bowel disturbance.
assessment: Urgently assess neurological level, sphincter symptoms and MRI when suspected.
caution: Progressive weakness, saddle symptoms or bladder dysfunction require emergency evaluation.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: spinal pathology
summary: Broad label for structural, inflammatory, vascular, neoplastic or degenerative spinal disease.
assessment: Localize spinal versus nerve-root findings; evaluate red flags and targeted imaging.
caution: Not a single diagnosis; cord compression is a critical cause to exclude.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Stereotypies
summary: Repetitive, patterned, seemingly purposeless movements often beginning in childhood.
assessment: Assess onset, triggers, suppressibility, developmental context and impairment.
caution: May occur in typical development or neurodevelopmental disorders; differ from tics and seizures.

name: Stimulant-induced mania
summary: Manic symptoms temporally related to stimulant exposure or intoxication.
assessment: Review substances, dose, timing, persistence after cessation and past independent mood episodes.
caution: Distinguish substance-induced syndrome from bipolar disorder; urgent assessment if severe agitation or psychosis.

name: stroke
summary: Sudden brain injury due to interrupted blood flow or bleeding.
assessment: Urgent stroke assessment, last-known-well time and neuroimaging.
caution: An emergency even when symptoms improve; ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke require different treatment.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Substance use disorder
summary: Problematic pattern of substance use causing clinically significant impairment or distress.
assessment: Assess impaired control, risky use, social effects, tolerance/withdrawal when relevant and severity.
caution: Physical dependence alone is not necessarily a substance use disorder.

name: substance-induced mood symptoms
summary: Depressive or manic symptoms attributable to intoxication, withdrawal or medication exposure.
assessment: Assess timing, pharmacology, persistence and independent mood episodes.
caution: Temporal association alone may not establish causation.

name: substance-induced psychosis
summary: Hallucinations or delusions associated with substance intoxication, withdrawal or medication effects.
assessment: Assess toxicology context, timeline, delirium, safety and medical mimics.
caution: Symptoms that persist beyond expected substance effects may require evaluation for primary psychosis.

name: substance-induced psychotic disorder
summary: Formal diagnostic category for prominent psychosis caused by substance or medication exposure.
assessment: Establish causative exposure, timing, exclusion of delirium and independent psychotic disorders.
caution: Not every intoxication-related perceptual change meets disorder criteria.

name: substance-related amnesia
summary: Memory impairment associated with intoxication, withdrawal or long-term neurotoxic effects.
assessment: Assess substance history, nutritional deficiency, neurological causes and cognitive pattern.
caution: Thiamine deficiency and Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome are important in alcohol-related cases.

name: syncope
summary: Transient loss of consciousness due to brief global cerebral hypoperfusion, usually with rapid recovery.
assessment: Assess posture, prodrome, ECG, orthostatic vitals, exertional events and cardiac risk.
caution: Can resemble seizure; exertional syncope or abnormal ECG needs urgent evaluation.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Thyroid eye disease
summary: Autoimmune orbital inflammation often associated with Graves disease, causing proptosis, diplopia and eye irritation.
assessment: Assess vision, color vision, eye movements, cornea, thyroid function and orbital imaging when needed.
caution: Vision-threatening optic neuropathy or corneal exposure needs urgent specialist care.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: TIA
summary: Transient ischemic attack: temporary focal neurological dysfunction caused by ischemia without acute infarction.
assessment: Urgent stroke/TIA assessment, vascular and cardiac workup and brain imaging.
caution: A warning event with early stroke risk; resolution of symptoms does not make it harmless.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: tick paralysis
summary: Acute ascending flaccid weakness caused by neurotoxin from an attached tick.
assessment: Examine skin and scalp for ticks; assess breathing, reflexes and differential.
caution: Removal of the tick can reverse symptoms; respiratory failure is possible.

sources.title: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — Health Topics
U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: toxic-metabolic causes
summary: Broad differential category for neurological or psychiatric symptoms due to toxins, drugs or systemic metabolic derangements.
assessment: Assess medication/exposure history, glucose, electrolytes, renal/hepatic function and infection when relevant.
caution: Not a specific diagnosis; identify the responsible process.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: toxic-metabolic encephalopathy
summary: Diffuse brain dysfunction due to systemic metabolic abnormalities, organ failure, drugs or toxins.
assessment: Assess mental status, glucose, electrolytes, renal/liver tests, oxygenation and medication exposures.
caution: Often causes global inattention and fluctuating cognition; focal signs suggest additional pathology.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Transient global amnesia
summary: Abrupt temporary inability to form new memories with preserved identity and other neurological functions.
assessment: Assess witnessed repetitive questioning, duration, focal deficits, seizure and vascular alternatives.
caution: Typically resolves within 24 hours; atypical presentations require urgent evaluation.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: trigeminal neuralgia
summary: Brief recurrent electric-shock facial pain in trigeminal distribution, often triggered by innocuous stimuli.
assessment: Assess pain distribution, sensory exam, triggers and MRI when indicated.
caution: Continuous numbness or other cranial deficits suggest secondary causes.

name: ulnar neuropathy
summary: Entrapment or injury of ulnar nerve causing numbness in ring/small fingers and intrinsic hand weakness.
assessment: Assess elbow/wrist compression, motor exam and nerve conduction studies when indicated.
caution: Distinguish from C8/T1 radiculopathy and generalized neuropathy.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: vestibular injury
summary: Damage or dysfunction of peripheral or central balance pathways causing vertigo or imbalance.
assessment: Assess timing, triggers, hearing, eye movements and neurological red flags.
caution: Acute continuous vertigo with central signs may represent posterior circulation stroke.

sources.title: U.S. National Library of Medicine — MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia

name: Viral meningitis
summary: Inflammation of meninges caused by a virus, often producing fever, headache and neck stiffness.
assessment: Assess illness severity, CSF when indicated and exclude bacterial meningitis or encephalitis.
caution: Clinical features alone may not safely distinguish viral from bacterial meningitis.
